provenance.instrument: Borough of Downingtown Zoning Ordinance of 1989 (Chapter 287 Zoning, Ord. No. 89-14 of 10-11-1989, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 DO0156, Borough of Downingtown. The definitions name the East Lancaster Avenue National Register district and Chester County records, and the zoning hearing notice goes to the Chester County Planning Commission (287-7, 287-142B), so this is Downingtown borough, Chester County. District use lists and area and bulk rules are text in Articles V to XV. The attachments are a planting table and sign appendices. The Floodplain District is governed by Chapter 150, which 287-12 incorporates. New Laws: none (0)
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 table of contents: 'Includes legislation through 07-01-2026.' New Laws (0). 287-76 and 150-6.02 carry Ord. No. 2026-03 of 7-1-2026
checks: The code has no accessory dwelling unit use. The words searched (accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, garage apartment, second dwelling, ECHO, extended family, elder cottage, tenant house, temporary dwelling, living quarters, caretaker, conversion) find only the conversion of dwellings (287-94), the conversion and group home definitions and other uses. No residential district lists an ADU (287-19, 287-23, 287-27, 287-32)

Each district lists its principal uses 'and no other', and permits as accessory uses only 'Uses customarily accessory and incidental to' residential uses, home occupations and pools (287-19B, 287-23B, 287-27B, 287-32B). A dwelling unit is for 'occupancy by only one family' with no enclosed space in common with another unit except halls and porches (287-7). No general rule for uses not provided for was found in the parts read

Conversion of dwellings: a single-family detached dwelling in R-3, R-4 or C-1 that existed on the chapter's effective date (10-11-1989) may become two units by special exception, only in a building with at least 3,000 sq ft of floor area on that date. Two parking spaces per unit, the two-family area and bulk rules of the district, no outside change except for safety, and each new unit at least 500 sq ft (287-94, 287-27C(6), 287-32C(7))

Two-family dwellings (twin or duplex) are permitted by right in R-3 and R-4: 5,000 sq ft per family in R-3 and 4,000 sq ft per family in R-4, 70 ft wide for a duplex (287-28B, 287-33B). That is a building for two units. Turning the existing house into two units is a conversion
R-1 and R-2 permit only the single-family detached dwelling as a house (287-19A, 287-23A)

Accessory buildings: 3 ft from side and rear lot lines and 5 ft from the edge of any alley or street at the side or rear (287-20I, 287-24I, 287-28E, 287-33F). A private garage may be at most 15 ft tall (287-74). Garden sheds and similar uninhabitable structures at most 12 ft (287-73E)

Lot coverage is split: a maximum building coverage and a separate 'Maximum other impervious surface coverage' for paving (287-20, 287-24, 287-28, 287-33). Lot area excludes rights-of-way and, where they make up more than 20% of the lot, floodplain, slopes over 20%, high water table soils and wetlands (287-7 'Lot area')

Parking: 'Single-family, two-family, quadraplex and townhouse dwellings: two parking spaces for each dwelling unit'. A fraction of one-half space or less is disregarded (287-107A, D(1)(a)). Parking areas may cover no more than 50% of any required yard (287-103C)

Floodplain District (Chapter 150 through 287-12): 'Within any identified floodplain area, any new construction, except storage sheds, decks, and fences constructed in compliance with Subsection E, F, and G below, shall be prohibited', unless a variance is granted under Article IX (150-6.02, Ord. No. 2026-03). In an AE zone without a floodway, no new construction or development within 50 ft landward of the top of bank without a DEP permit (150-5.02B(2)(b)). An accessory structure in the floodplain may not be designed or used for human habitation and may have no sanitary facilities (150-6.02E). No expansion of an existing building may raise the base flood elevation, and work of 50% or more of market value is a substantial improvement (150-8.02). Variances are limited in Article IX, which was read only in part

Steep Slope Conservation District (slopes of 20% or more): a single-family detached dwelling only by special exception, and impervious cover in the district at most half the base district maximum (287-13E(3), (4)). No structure on soils with a seasonally high water table within one foot of the surface (287-14A). Wetlands need a delineation and any required permits (287-14B)

Nonconforming lots: a vacant lot of record may be built on if the yards are met, else by special exception, but not if it is under half the required area or width (287-125A). A nonconforming structure may be extended by up to 25% of its floor area on the effective date if the extension meets the area and bulk rules (287-124C)

Overlays not read in full: Central Business Revitalization, Adaptive Reuse/Mixed-Use, Mixed-Use, Traditional Neighborhood Development, Uptown Transportation Development, Kardon Park Redevelopment, Woodbine and the Historic Resources Overlay (the East Lancaster Avenue National Register district, 287-101.3). They may add uses or design rules
Variances: Zoning Hearing Board on the findings of MPC 910.2 (287-144A). No bar on a use variance was found
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Downingtown Borough Zoning Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360 (print view), one page at a time, on 2026-11-17. Read: 287-5.1, 287-7 up to 'Porch' (later definitions by element only), Article III, Article IV, Articles V to VIII, 287-94, Article XVI, Article XVIII, Article XX, Article XXII and Chapter 150 up to 150-8.02F (Article IX variances and the 150-10.02 definitions only by element snippets), and code searches. Not read: 287-1 to 287-5, 287-6, Articles IX to XVD (C-1, C-2, C-3, I-1, I-2, I-3, OS, P, R/C and the overlays), Article XVII except 287-94, Article XIX, Article XXI, Article XXIII, and the rest of 287-7 and Chapter 150. A search for the rule on uses not provided for returned a site error. Open points: whether the code has a general rule for uses not provided for (none found in Articles I to VIII, XVI, XVIII, XX and XXII), the C-1 lot figures for a conversion (the C-1 article was not read), and whether 150-6.02 bars an addition to an existing house in the floodplain (read as reaching only new construction).

status.note: No residential district lists a second unit on a house lot. R-3 and R-4 permit two-family dwellings by right, and R-3, R-4 and C-1 permit the conversion of a large older house into two units by special exception (287-94)

path.note: A second unit on a house lot is not a listed use, and each district lists its uses 'and no other', so the path is a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board (MPC 910.2). R-3 and R-4 permit two-family dwellings by right, and a large older house may be converted into two units by special exception (see the other paths)

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board on the findings of MPC 910.2. No bar on a use variance

value.name: Conversion of a single-family detached dwelling (R-3, R-4, C-1)
value.conditions: A single-family detached dwelling that existed on 10-11-1989 converted into two units, each with its own kitchen, bath and sleeping space. The building had at least 3,000 sq ft of floor area on that date. Two parking spaces per unit with direct access to a street or alley. The two-family area and bulk rules of the district apply (5,000 sq ft per family in R-3, 4,000 sq ft per family in R-4, 70 ft wide for a duplex). No outside change except for safety, and fire escapes at the rear where practicable. Each new unit at least 500 sq ft

disputed_by.note: Improvements to an existing building are governed by 150-8.02, which allows an expansion that does not raise the base flood elevation. Whether an addition to the house is new construction under 150-6.02 is not settled

value.condition: In the floodplain any construction or development needs a permit. No expansion of an existing building may raise the base flood elevation, and work of 50% or more of the building's market value is a substantial improvement. An accessory structure in the floodplain may not be designed or used for human habitation.

In an AE zone without a floodway 'No new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse, unless the appropriate permit is obtained from the Department of Environmental Protection's regional office'.

Steep Slope Conservation District (slopes of 20% or more): a single-family detached dwelling only by special exception, and impervious cover in the district at most half the base district maximum. A Borough Engineer review of slope, grading and drainage plans comes first.
No structure may be built on soils whose seasonally high water table is within one foot of the surface (Linside silt loam excepted).
